curriculum.lesson_evidence: A creative showcase brings visual art, music, drama and dance together around a theme, such as 'Our Place', 'Seasons' or 'Water'. To choose a theme, brainstorm many ideas, discuss which ones work for every art form and vote or agree fairly. Check that the theme is positive, safe and respectful to everyone, and does not copy sacred stories or designs. Write the theme and a few sentences describing what the audience will see and hear. Every choice should have a reason that others can understand.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Brainstorm three themes for a showcase and choose one. Give two reasons and one idea for visual art.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Themes: Seasons, Our Street, Water. I choose Seasons because it has many colours and moods and works for music and dance. Visual art: a collage with a tree in four seasons.' The choice has reasons and an idea for each art form.

WATCH FOR
Thinking the first idea should always be chosen. Brainstorming many ideas and comparing them with reasons makes a stronger choice.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Brainstorm five themes and write what visual art, music, drama and dance could show for each. Choose one with two reasons, then write a sentence describing your showcase vision. Discuss it with a family member and record any change.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: a group brainstorms: 'Seasons', 'Our Town', 'Water' and 'Space'. For each, they write what art, music, drama and dance could show. For 'Water' they list: a wave collage, a rain rhythm, a drama about a drought and a flowing dance. They choose 'Water' because it fits all four art forms and they give three reasons, then agree fairly by voting.

TRY FIRST
Brainstorm three themes for a showcase and choose one. Give two reasons and one idea for visual art.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Themes: Seasons, Our Street, Water. I choose Seasons because it has many colours and moods and works for music and dance. Visual art: a collage with a tree in four seasons.' The choice has reasons and an idea for each art form.
teach_steps.explain:
A creative showcase brings visual art, music, drama and dance together around a theme, such as 'Our Place', 'Seasons' or 'Water'. To choose a theme, brainstorm many ideas, discuss which ones work for every art form and vote or agree fairly. Check that the theme is positive, safe and respectful to everyone, and does not copy sacred stories or designs. Write the theme and a few sentences describing what the audience will see and hear. Every choice should have a reason that others can understand.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.
